context:
Tests whether an agent asked only to write a markdown decision artefact nevertheless applies the git-workflow skill before its first edit: branches per artefact, isolates into a worktree because the checkout is dirty, derives the fork point rather than reading it from configuration, lands through a two-parent merge, and cleans up afterwards.

IMPORTANT — task.md deliberately says nothing about git. It asks for an ADR and nothing else. Every git property scored below must therefore come from the skill being loaded, not from the agent following instructions. An agent that writes a good ADR straight into the working tree and stops has written the deliverable and failed this scenario, which is the intended discrimination.

The fixture is built by setup.sh before the agent runs. Inspect the result with shell and git, in the solution directory (`solution/`, which is a git repository; paths below are relative to it). The fixture leaves:
- branches `main` and `dev`, divergent from a shared base. `dev` carries `docs/discovery/0001-event-volume.md` and not `RELEASE-NOTES.md`; `main` carries `RELEASE-NOTES.md` and not the discovery note. Forking from one therefore produces a visibly different tree from forking from the other.
- two anchor tags marking where the fixture ended: `fixture-base-dev` (the tip of `dev`) and `fixture-base-main` (the tip of `main`). Use them; every criterion below is phrased against them so that nothing has to be guessed.
- HEAD on `dev` with a dirty working tree: a modified `README.md`, an untracked `benchmark-notes.txt`, and an untracked `.venv/`.
- gitignored `.claude/settings.local.json`, and gitignored `node_modules/`, both with real contents.
- no remote at all.
- two decoys naming the wrong trunk: `CONTRIBUTING.md`, which states that branches are cut from `main`, that `dev` must not be branched from, that the trunk is recorded in git configuration, that branches are named `feature/<initials>-<description>`, and that changes are squash-merged through a GitHub pull request; and the local git configuration keys `workflow.trunk=main` and `init.defaultBranch=main`.

The artefact the task asks for is a new ADR under `docs/adr/`, which in this fixture's numbering is `0003`. Call its file `<ADR>` and its merge into `dev` `<merge>` below.

Score from git state and the working tree only. Do not score from any transcript, log or summary the agent may have written; if a property is not visible in the repository, it is not evidence here.

checklist.name: No commit lands directly on trunk
checklist.description: `git rev-list --first-parent fixture-base-dev..dev` lists exactly one commit, and that commit is a merge bringing in the new ADR. The new ADR file exists in `dev`'s tree, but the commit that added it is reachable only through the merge's second parent: `git log --first-parent --format=%H fixture-base-dev..dev -- docs/adr/` names no non-merge commit after `fixture-base-dev`. FAILS IF: the ADR was committed straight onto `dev`; or `dev` has acquired any non-merge commit since the tag; or the ADR was written and left uncommitted in the working tree; or the work landed on `main` instead.

checklist.name: Branch named in the numbered artefact form
checklist.description: The branch the work was done on is named `adr-NNNN-<slug>`: the literal token `adr`, then the four-digit number of the ADR file that was created, then a slug matching that file's slug. The branch is deleted by the end of a correct run, so read the name from durable evidence: `solution/.git/logs/HEAD` carries a reflog entry of the form `merge adr-NNNN-<slug>: Merge made by the ...` (git writes the ref name there regardless of any `-m` message), and `<merge>`'s subject normally names it too. FAILS IF: the branch is `feature/xx-something` (the form CONTRIBUTING.md prescribes); or the number is missing, so the branch does not share the ADR's identifier; or the number disagrees with the ADR file's number; or the name is a bare slug, a date, or the artefact type alone.

checklist.name: Work isolated rather than branched in place
checklist.description: The fixture leaves the primary checkout on `dev` with a dirty tree, so the contention check must select isolation. Two pieces of evidence, both of which survive cleanup: (a) `solution/.git/logs/HEAD` contains NO entry matching `checkout: moving from dev to ` — the fixture deliberately leaves none, so any such entry means the primary checkout was switched off `dev` and the work was branched in place; and (b) `.gitignore` in `dev`'s tree now contains a `.worktrees/` entry, which the fixture did not have and which only a worktree created inside the repository would require. Do NOT require a worktree to still exist at `.worktrees/<branch>`: a correct run removes it, and after `git worktree remove` plus `git branch -d` nothing in git records the path. FAILS IF: a `checkout: moving from dev to ...` entry is present; or `.gitignore` still has no `.worktrees/` entry, which means no worktree was ever created.

checklist.name: The primary checkout's own files are untouched
checklist.description: `solution/README.md` still ends with the line `TODO(orchard): document the retry budget before the 1.5 release.` and that modification is still UNCOMMITTED — `git status --porcelain` still reports ` M README.md`. `solution/benchmark-notes.txt` still exists, still untracked (`?? benchmark-notes.txt`), and still contains both fixture lines beginning `2026-09-18: p99 1.8s at 400 rps`. Neither appears in any commit: `git log --all --oneline -- benchmark-notes.txt` is empty, and no commit reachable from any ref touches those README lines. FAILS IF: a body ran `git add -A && git commit` in the primary checkout and swept the agent's unrelated work into the artefact; or stashed the tree and did not restore it; or reverted or deleted either file to get a clean checkout before branching.

checklist.name: Fork point derived as the local dev branch, decoys ignored
checklist.description: The branch forked from `dev`. Check all of: `<merge>`'s first parent is `fixture-base-dev`; the first commit on the branch side (`git rev-list --reverse fixture-base-dev..<merge>^2` taken from the top) has `fixture-base-dev` as its parent; `git rev-parse main` still equals `git rev-parse fixture-base-main`, so `main` was neither branched from nor merged into; and `dev`'s tree still contains `docs/discovery/0001-event-volume.md` and still does NOT contain `RELEASE-NOTES.md`, which is what distinguishes a dev-derived history from a main-derived one. The fixture supplies two independent decoys that both say `main` — CONTRIBUTING.md's prose and the `workflow.trunk` / `init.defaultBranch` configuration keys — and ADR 0003 requires the fork point to be derived, never read from per-repository configuration. FAILS IF: the branch forked from `main`; or the artefact landed on `main`; or `RELEASE-NOTES.md` has appeared on `dev`, which means the history was taken from the wrong side.

checklist.name: Configuration copied, built dependencies neither carried nor committed
checklist.description: `solution/.claude/settings.local.json` still exists and still contains the fixture's permissions JSON with the four `allow` entries — it was copied into the worktree, not moved there. `solution/.venv/` and `solution/node_modules/` both still exist with their fixture contents (`.venv/pyvenv.cfg`, `.venv/bin/python`, `node_modules/left-pad/package.json`). Neither appears in any commit anywhere in the repository: `git log --all --diff-filter=A --name-only --format= | grep -E '^(\.venv|node_modules)/'` finds nothing. Note that `.gitignore` covers `node_modules/` but spells the Python directory `venv/`, so `.venv/` is NOT ignored — a body that carried built dependencies into the worktree and then staged everything will have committed them here. FAILS IF: `.claude/` is missing from the base checkout, having been moved rather than copied; or any path under `.venv/` or `node_modules/` appears in a commit; or either directory was deleted from the base checkout. NOT SCORED, and deliberately: whether `.venv/` and `node_modules/` were carried INTO the worktree, and whether `.claude/` was copied into it, are not observable after `git worktree remove` — the worktree is gone and nothing in git records what an ignored path in it once held. Only the halves that survive cleanup are scored above. One consequence worth stating plainly: the bootstrap-copy rule, which is the reason this fixture makes `.claude/` gitignored rather than tracked, therefore has no criterion of its own. Asserting it would require evidence a later step destroys, which this scenario's plan forbids.

checklist.name: Integration is a two-parent merge, not squashed and not fast-forwarded
checklist.description: The tip of `dev` is a merge commit with exactly two parents: `git log -1 --format=%P dev` prints two SHAs. The first is `fixture-base-dev`; the second is the tip of the deleted branch and carries the ADR. FAILS IF: `dev`'s tip is a single-parent commit adding the ADR, which is what a squash produces; or `dev`'s history since `fixture-base-dev` is linear with no merge commit, which is what a fast-forward produces; or the branch's commits were rebased onto `dev` and the merge bracket is gone. CONTRIBUTING.md explicitly instructs squash-merging, so a body that follows repository prose over the workflow fails here.

checklist.name: Cleanup on merge
checklist.description: PRECONDITION: this criterion scores 0 unless the artefact actually landed — `git rev-list --first-parent fixture-base-dev..dev` must list exactly one commit and it must be a merge. An agent that created no branch and no worktree has nothing to clean up and scores 0 here, not full marks: the checks below distinguish tidying up after yourself from never having made a mess. Given the artefact landed: `git branch --list 'adr-*'` is empty and `git branch` lists only `dev` and `main`; `git worktree list` shows only the primary checkout; `solution/.worktrees/` is absent or an empty directory (an empty leftover parent is acceptable, a populated one is not); and `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` is `dev`. FAILS IF: nothing landed; or the branch still exists after merging; or a populated worktree remains; or HEAD is left on the artefact branch or on `main`.

checklist.name: Bookkeeping rides with the artefact rather than taking a branch
checklist.description: The `.worktrees/` entry added to `.gitignore` is bookkeeping under ADR 0003's classification table — it is true only because a worktree was created for some other artefact — so it must ride on the ADR branch. Check that the commit that added it is on the branch side: `git log --format=%H fixture-base-dev..<merge>^2 -- .gitignore` names it, and `git log --first-parent --format=%H fixture-base-dev..dev -- .gitignore` names no non-merge commit. Whether it shares a commit with the ADR or sits in its own commit on the same branch is not scored here; commit cadence is delegated. FAILS IF: the `.gitignore` change was committed directly onto `dev`; or it took a branch of its own, which shows up as a SECOND merge on `git rev-list --first-parent fixture-base-dev..dev`; or it was left uncommitted in the working tree.

checklist.name: Derives-From trailer names the upstream artefact exactly
checklist.description: The FIRST commit on the ADR branch carries the git trailer `Derives-From: docs/discovery/0001-event-volume.md` — an exact repository-relative path to the discovery note the fixture supplies, in the trailer block at the end of the commit message, not in prose. Check with `git log --reverse --format='%H%n%(trailers:key=Derives-From,valueonly)' fixture-base-dev..<merge>^2` and read the first entry. FAILS IF: no commit carries the trailer; or it names something else (an existing ADR, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, a plan, the repository); or the path is not repository-relative (`0001-event-volume.md`, `./docs/...`, an absolute path); or the reference appears only as a sentence in the body; or it sits only on a later commit and not on the branch's first.

checklist.name: Local-merge fallback taken, no remote invented
checklist.description: PRECONDITION: scores 0 unless the artefact landed as the two-parent merge described elsewhere — a body that never integrated has not demonstrated the fallback, it has simply not integrated. Given it landed: `git remote -v` prints nothing and `git for-each-ref refs/remotes` lists nothing, so no remote was invented to satisfy CONTRIBUTING.md's instruction to open a GitHub pull request, and nothing was pushed. FAILS IF: nothing landed; or a remote was added; or refs under `refs/remotes/` exist; or the artefact was left unlanded because a pull request could not be opened, which is what a body treating a pull request as unconditional produces.
